name: Coding Club
tagline: Crafting code, building solutions, and conquering hackathons.
description: The Coding Club is the campus hub for software engineers, competitive programmers, and open-source enthusiasts. From beginners learning Python to advanced developers building scalable full-stack applications, we provide peer mentorship, weekly code sprints, and hackathon preparation.

lead.faculty_advisor: Dr. Sarah Jenkins (Dept. of Computer Science & Engineering)

membership.eligibility: Open to all enrolled undergraduate and postgraduate students from any department.
membership.prerequisites: None! Beginners are warmly welcomed with dedicated starter tracks.

activities: Weekly 'Code & Coffee' algorithmic problem-solving sessions (LeetCode/Codeforces)
Full-Stack Web & Mobile App development workshops (React, Node, Flask, Flutter)
Open-Source Contribution Month (Hacktoberfest campus drive)
Internal 24-hour hackathons and mentorship for national competitions

events.title: CodeStorm 2026 - Annual 36-Hour Hackathon
events.description: Flagship university hackathon with prize pool of $3,000, sponsor booths, and industry judges.

events.title: Git & GitHub Crash Course for Freshers
events.description: Hands-on session on version control, branching, pull requests, and collaborative coding.

registration.process: Fill out the online Google Form on the student portal or visit during our Wednesday weekly meetups.
registration.deadline: Rolling admissions throughout the academic year; core team recruitment closes October 31st.
registration.orientation: Fall Orientation on October 20th in Auditorium B.

name: AI/ML Club
tagline: Demystifying Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning.
description: The AI/ML Club explores the frontiers of Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Large Language Models, and Computer Vision. We host paper reading groups, hands-on Kaggle competitions, guest talks by AI researchers, and build community-driven AI applications.

lead.president: Priya Patel (Third Year, Data Science & AI)
lead.faculty_advisor: Prof. David Vance (Department of AI & Robotics)

membership.eligibility: Open to all students interested in artificial intelligence, mathematics, or data analytics.
membership.prerequisites: Basic understanding of high school math or beginner Python is helpful, but introductory tracks are provided.

activities: Hands-on Machine Learning pipelines with Scikit-Learn, PyTorch, and TensorFlow
Generative AI & LLM Prompt Engineering bootcamps
Kaggle team sprints and data visualization contests
Weekly AI Paper Reading Group covering cutting-edge research from arXiv

events.title: Datathon 2026: Campus Predictive Modeling Challenge
events.description: 48-hour competitive data science challenge with real-world healthcare and climate datasets.

events.title: Industry Guest Lecture: Future of Autonomous Agents
events.description: Keynote by Google DeepMind Research Scientist on multi-agent reasoning systems.

registration.process: Register via the college AI Club portal or sign up at the AI Center bulletin desk.
registration.deadline: Open registrations all year round; project groups form in October.
registration.orientation: Orientation and hands-on Colab setup on October 22nd at 5:30 PM.

name: Robotics Club
tagline: Bringing code to life through circuits, sensors, and mechanical design.
description: The Robotics Club bridges mechanical engineering, electronics, and embedded programming. Members design, 3D print, solder, and program autonomous robots, drones, and combat bots for university showdowns and national competitions like Robocon.

lead.faculty_advisor: Dr. Elena Rostova (Dept. of Electrical Engineering)

membership.eligibility: Open to all students. We need coders, 3D designers, electronics hobbyists, and strategists.
membership.fee: $10 per semester (Covers consumable electronics, soldering supplies, and 3D printing filament)
membership.prerequisites: No prior experience needed; basic safety training is conducted during week one.

activities: Arduino and Raspberry Pi embedded systems prototyping
3D CAD modeling (SolidWorks / Fusion 360) and 3D printing components
Autonomous maze-solver and line-follower robot build challenges
Combat robotics workshop (1lb and 3lb beetleweight bots)

events.title: RoboWars & Line Follower Championship
events.description: High-octane campus combat bot tournament and precision autonomous navigation race.

events.title: IoT & Smart Home Automation Bootcamp
events.description: Build your own WiFi-enabled weather station and smart lamp with ESP32.

registration.process: Visit the Makerspace Lab B08 in person or complete the registration form online.
registration.deadline: Fall intake closes November 10th for national team allocations.
registration.orientation: Makerspace Walkthrough & Safety Training on October 25th at 4:30 PM.

name: Cultural Club
tagline: Celebrating diversity, rhythm, creativity, and the performing arts.
description: The Cultural Club is the artistic heartbeat of the university. It brings together musicians, dancers, actors, photographers, visual artists, and poets. We organize the annual college cultural fest, open mic evenings, theatrical plays, and festive celebrations.

lead.faculty_advisor: Prof. Arthur Pendelton (Faculty of Arts & Humanities)

membership.eligibility: All students passionate about performing arts, fine arts, stage management, or creative expression.
membership.prerequisites: Enthusiasm and passion. Auditions are conducted only for select stage production roles; general club membership is open to all.

activities: Western & Classical music band jams and vocal training
Choreography workshops (Contemporary, Hip-hop, Folk, Bollywood)
Street plays (Nukkad Natak) and stage theater drama rehearsals
Monthly acoustic Open Mic nights for stand-up comedy, poetry, and storytelling
Canvas painting, digital art, and photography exhibitions

events.title: Spring Fest 'Rhythm & Canvas' 2027
events.description: Three-day university cultural extravaganza featuring celebrity concert, Battle of the Bands, and fashion parade.

events.title: Autumn Acoustic Unplugged & Open Mic
events.description: Cozy autumn evening of student acoustic sets, spoken word, and hot cider.

registration.process: Submit your creative interest form on the Student Union site or attend an open practice session on Monday.
registration.deadline: Open registrations year-round; auditions for the annual play close November 1st.
registration.orientation: Welcome Jam & Icebreaker evening on October 18th in Student Center 201.

name: Sports Club
tagline: Fostering teamwork, endurance, discipline, and athletic excellence.
description: The Sports Club coordinates intramural tournaments, varsity team practices, and general fitness sessions across campus. Whether you are training for competitive inter-university championships or simply looking to stay active, our club provides equipment, coaching, and spirited leagues.

lead.president: Rohan Deshmukh (Final Year, Physical Education & Management)
lead.faculty_advisor: Coach Michael Torres (Director of Campus Athletics)

meeting_schedule.day: Every Monday to Friday (Practice Sessions) & Saturday Matches
meeting_schedule.venue: University Sports Complex, Gymnasium, & Football Field

membership.eligibility: Open to all enrolled students with valid college ID and sports complex access.
membership.fee: Free for general intramurals and gym access; specialized equipment rental may require a refundable deposit.
membership.prerequisites: Medical fitness clearance required for varsity team tryouts.

activities: Intramural tournaments in Football (Soccer), Cricket, Basketball, Volleyball, and Badminton
Indoor games club: Chess, Table Tennis, Carrom, and Esports
Morning fitness bootcamp, yoga sessions, and strength conditioning
Inter-collegiate athletic meets and marathon training

events.title: Inter-Department Athletic League 2026
events.description: Week-long sporting clashes between college departments competing for the Chancellor's Trophy.

events.title: Campus 5K Midnight Run for Mental Health
events.description: Annual neon night run with glow sticks, hydration stations, and finisher medals.

registration.process: Register in person at the Sports Complex reception desk or submit your sports preference form online.
registration.deadline: Intramural league team rosters lock on November 15th; recreational memberships open continuously.
registration.orientation: Sports Fest & Fitness Assessment Day on October 21st at 5:00 PM at the Gymnasium.
